nodes.question: What have several studies investigated to improve SSI teaching?
nodes.answer: Several studies have investigated how to effectively improve teachers' professional development (PD) for SSI teaching.
nodes.paragraph: Moreover, SSI education focuses on developing students ethical reasoning and character, promoting decision-making based on moral judgments through engagement in public discourse and argumentation (Zei- dler, 2014). Research in Science Education Various factors bring challenges to SSI teaching for teachers. The lack of pedagogical content knowledge and instructional confidence is one of the barriers influencing teachers willingness to teach SSI (Kinskey & Zeidler, 2024). Due to lower confidence in discuss- ing controversial issues, teachers usually feel unprepared to balance subject content and ethical discussions, especially in areas with sociocultural and religious conflicts (Relela & Mavuru, 2023). Moreover, teachers often adopt a neutral or value-free stance in the classroom to avoid controversy and perceptions of indoctrination, stemming from concerns about maintaining neutrality (Ozcan-Ermis & Herv , 2024). Additionally, practical chal- lenges like limited curriculum time, scarce resources specific to SSI instruction, and diffi- culties in assessing student learning in these areas further complicate SSI teaching (Nielsen et al., 2020). To overcome teachers pedagogical challenges, several studies have investigated how to effectively improve teachers professional development (PD) for SSI teaching (Bayram- Jacobs et al., 2019; Friedrichsen et al., 2020; Kinskey & Zeidler, 2024; Leung, 2022).

nodes.label: Education
nodes.question: What do the PD programs mentioned in the paragraph help teachers to do?
nodes.answer: The PD programs help teachers incorporate Socially Significant Issues (SSIs) into their curricula by promoting collaborative design and reflective practices.
nodes.paragraph: These PD programs can help teachers incorporate SSIs into their curricula by promoting collaborative design and reflective practices (Authors, 2022a; Friedrichsen et al., 2020; Kinskey & Zeidler, 2024; Leung, 2022). These studies highlighted the role of interac- tion and reflection in PD programs and focused on teachers beliefs, pedagogical content knowledge, attributes, or epistemic frames related to effective SSI teaching or qualitative lesson planning. The use of written surveys and semi-structured interviews in these studies ignored the progression of teachers epistemic frames during the PD program. Therefore, we examined changes in discourse and interaction in a PD program to elucidate teachers development for SSI teaching. Literature Review SSI Teaching and PD in Education Given the strong focus on cultivating student competence, SSI teaching and learning have received increasing attention in both classrooms and academia. For example, in Taiwan the Curriculum Guidelines of 12-year Basic Education merit attention to cultivating stu- dents core competencies and encouraging them to become life-long learners who can solve common daily problems as well as future challenges (Ministry of Education, 2021). Considering SSI as one of the daily and future challenges that students must overcome, the curriculum guidelines for natural science further emphasize infusing SSI into the curricu- lum through multiple methods such as inquiry-based learning and project-based learning (Ministry of Education, 2018).

nodes.question: What is suggested to enhance teacher training in environmental education?
nodes.answer: It is suggested to enhance teacher training by ensuring teachers feel competent and confident in introducing environmental education programs.
nodes.paragraph: Different stud - ies have highlighted the importance of teacher training in environmental issues as a crucial component to ensure that teachers in their professional future may approach socio-environmental sustainability competences with their students (Varela-Losada et al., 2019 ). Nevertheless, previous studies have also reported deficiencies regard - ing education for sustainable development and socio-environmental topics in initial teacher training (Morote et al., 2021 ), as well as among teachers in service (Borg et al., 2013 ). There is clear evidence of the need to enhance teacher training in these areas, ensuring they feel both competent and confident in introducing environmental education programs. This will help foster behaviours that promote interaction with and care for the environment, as well as environmentally friendly values, beliefs, and attitudes. In this sense, the use of learning gardens in the university system as teach - ing resources could play an important role in fostering these values in initial teacher training (V zquez-Verdera & Esc mez-S inchez, 2022 ). The basis of current environmental problems lies in people S environmental cul - ture (Moyano-Diaz et al., 2011 ).
